title: The Practice
author: Seth Godin
blurb: Seth Godin argues that creative work is not reserved for a lucky few with special talent. It is a practice anyone can choose: a habit of showing up, doing the work, and sharing it, regardless of how it is received. He urges readers to trust the process rather than obsess over outcomes they cannot control. Godin treats fear, not lack of ideas, as the real obstacle behind blocks and perfectionism. He insists that good work is made for someone specific, to change something for them, which makes it an act of generosity. Professionals, in his view, ship on schedule, accept that their work is good enough for its purpose, and then do it again. The book is a short, encouraging push to stop waiting for permission and start making things that matter.

lessons.t: Creativity Is a Choice, Not a Gift
lessons.b: Creative work is not a talent some people are born with but a practice anyone can choose to commit to.
